What can Oh Agent connect to? Integrations and extension points

Oh Agent is built on the open-source Agent Vitals engine, and Agent City is its first app. The engine connects in two directions. Data comes in from agents’ local session logs: four built-in sources, extra folders you add, and local manifest sources. Data goes out only through narrow local interfaces: a stdio Data MCP server for your own AI agent, read-only projections for built-in plugins such as Agent City, and file exports you start by hand. Everything below exists in the code on the dev branch at commit bf7196a unless it’s in the Roadmap section.

What exists today

Section titled “What exists today”
Integration Direction Who uses it Status
Claude Code In Everyone Built in
Codex In Everyone Built in
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) In Everyone Built in
WorkBuddy In Everyone Built in (usage; fewer behaviour checks)
Extra folders In Users with logs in other places Desktop Settings, for Claude Code, Codex and DSH
Manifest sources In Users of agents without built-in support CLI and desktop; local import only, official catalog empty
Skill auditor In (skills) Users auditing installed Agent Skills Agent skill, DSH bundle, CLI
Data MCP server Out Your local AI agent (stdio MCP client) agent-vitals data-mcp serve
Built-in plugins Out (inside the app) Contributors building views like City Official, compiled in; no third-party install
Data export Out (files) Users, for backup or analysis data-export-private / data-export-redacted → one <harness>.jsonl per source
City photo and film export Out (files) Users, for sharing Native save dialog; stats overlay only, no excerpts

Which adapters exist in code?

Section titled “Which adapters exist in code?”

Each folder in crates/agent-vitals-harnesses/src/harnesses/ is one adapter:

Adapter folder Sessions and usage (city district) Behaviour findings Skill audit Docs
claude_code Yes Yes Yes Claude Code
codex Yes Yes Yes Codex
dsh Yes Yes Yes (agent/preset scopes) DeepSeek Harness
workbuddy Yes Not during sync Yes WorkBuddy
openclaw (also covers Hermes) No No Yes Skill auditor
generic (manifest sources) Yes, usage only No No Manifest sources

TBD: whether DSH has its own skill module. There’s no harnesses/dsh/skills/ folder; DSH skill scopes are described in HARNESS_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md.

Which one should I use?

Section titled “Which one should I use?”
  • You want your own AI agent to answer questions about your usage: use the Data MCP server.
  • Your Claude Code, Codex or DSH logs live somewhere else, such as a backup drive: add an extra folder.
  • Your agent isn’t supported but writes JSONL logs with token usage: write a manifest. No code needed.
  • You want full support for a new agent, including behaviour checks: add a data source in Rust and open a PR.
  • You want a new visual view on top of Agent Vitals data: see Built-in plugins.

Older integrations still in the repo

Section titled “Older integrations still in the repo”

Before Agent City, the project shipped a skill auditor, and it’s still in the repo: an agent skill (SKILL.md, packaged for ClawHub), a DSH bundle (integrations/dsh/), and CLI commands. OpenClaw and Hermes appear only there. See Skill auditor.

Roadmap / 规划中

Section titled “Roadmap / 规划中”

None of these are in the code at dev bf7196a. They are marked TBD until they ship.

  • TBD: Agents that help build your city (MCP). The idea is that your AI agent could help shape your city through MCP. Today’s Data MCP server can read usage data and change typed settings, but it has no tool that edits the city or its map.
  • TBD: Incremental hot update. Today a data change makes City reload the full projection and rebuild the whole scene, with a stable layout and growth animation (see Data pipeline). Sending only changed sessions and patching single buildings, Vite-style, isn’t implemented. The paged city:v3 (opt-in via ?cityData=v3) is a step toward it but still reloads everything.
  • TBD: City gallery (UGC). Sharing and browsing other people’s cities. There is no code for this in the repo.
  • TBD: Map editor for everyone. A city “repair” editor exists. Its first priorities (P0) were finished on 2026-10-12, but turning it into a product feature (removing developer switches, translations, onboarding) and importing/exporting map edits are scheduled for later (P3).
  • TBD: Official manifest catalog. The download channel and checks exist, but catalog/index.json has no entries yet.
  • Not promised: script adapters for manifests (P1.5), a manifest expression language (P2) and a community manifest catalog (P3) are design reservations, not commitments.
  • Assessed, not built: the repo has assessment notes for Cline, Pi and Hermes as session sources (docs/*_HARNESS_ASSESSMENT.md). TBD: whether any of them is planned.
